newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends slightly higher on crude, arb.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends slightly higher on crude, arb.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended slightly higher on Wednesday, continuing to draw support from steady crude oil values and arbitrage interest to the States, traders and brokers said.
"It's reasonably tight because stuff is going to the States," one broker said. "Theoretically (the arb) is still open."

Traders detected no heightened prompt demand in NWE due to delays at Algeria's Skikda port, which was still closed on Wednesday because of bad weather. A port official did not know when it would reopen.
Three cargoes delayed by the weather all had homes and one end-user was believed to have bought two cargoes late last week to alleviate some supply pressure.
"If it lasts for another week then yes you would see more buying," for prompt materials, the broker said.
Dec swaps finished 50 cents higher at $223.50 after earlier rising to $225.50. Jan swaps held at a $9 backwardation at $214/$215.
"I think naphtha is pretty crude sensitive right now," said another broker. "A five-cent move in crude means about a 50-cent move on naphtha."
A Russian cargo was sold late Tuesday at $222 cif into NWE but cargo prices on Wednesday ended at $224/$226.
Demand for heavier N+A grades was still seen lacklustre due to a negative naphtha/gasoline crack spread.
